prompt: A rectangle has vertices $(0, 0)$, $(5, 0)$, $(5, 3)$, $(0, 3)$. Find its **perimeter**.
hint: Perimeter is the total distance around the rectangle. The coordinates of the corners tell you how long each side is.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try the square with corners $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(1, 1)$, $(0, 1)$ first. Each side is $1$ unit, so its perimeter is $4$. This rectangle works the same way with longer sides.
Perimeter is the total distance around the rectangle. The coordinates of the corners tell you how long each side is.
The bottom side runs from $x = 0$ to $x = 5$, so the length is $5$. The right side runs from $y = 0$ to $y = 3$, so the width is $3$. A rectangle has two of each side.
Perimeter $= 2(5 + 3) = 16$, so the perimeter is $16$ units.

explanation: The side from $(0, 0)$ to $(5, 0)$ is horizontal, so its length is $|5 - 0| = 5$.
The side from $(5, 0)$ to $(5, 3)$ is vertical, so its length is $|3 - 0| = 3$.
Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so the perimeter is $2(5 + 3) = 2(8)$.
That gives $16$, so the perimeter is $16$ units.
